sources.title: High-yield savings accounts: Best rates and top picks for May 2026
sources.author: Angelica  Leicht
sources.excerpt: Today's high-yield savings accounts are offering hefty returns on your deposits. Here's where your money belongs now.
sources.text:
There are multiple, lucrative high-yield savings accounts for savers to consider this month. DAVID BENITO/DBenitostock/Getty Images
High interest savings accounts are once again drawing attention as interest rates remain elevated compared to just a few years ago. While the Federal Reserve has begun easing its benchmark rate, savers can still find competitive yields that significantly outperform traditional savings accounts. That makes this a critical moment for anyone holding cash to reconsider where their money sits.
At their core, high-yield savings accounts are designed to help your money grow faster without taking on market risk. These federally-insured deposit accounts typically offer rates far above the national average, which currently sits at just 0.38%, according to the FDIC. Today's top available high-yield savings rate, though, which is offered by Axos Bank, is substantially higher at 4.21%.
Still, not all high-yield savings accounts are created equal and the interest rate is just one factor worth weighing. Whether you're building an emergency fund, saving for a home or just looking to stop leaving money on the table, the question is which high-yield savings account is actually worth opening right now?

High-yield savings account rates: Key takeaways
• Current top APY: 4.21%
• Difference vs. national average: More than 10x higher
• FDIC/NCUA insured: Yes
• Rate type: Variable

The best high-yield savings accounts compared
Rates and information verified May 13, 2026. Note: Savings yields differ depending on the bank. Estimated earnings are rounded to the nearest whole number and assume the rate remains constant for one year. All savings account rates are variable and subject to change at any time.

Axos Bank
• APY: 4.21%*
• Minimum balance for APY: $1,500 avg daily balance + $1,500/mo direct deposit
• Access: Web/app; 90,000+ ATMs
• Est. Earnings on $10K (1 yr): $421
• Min. Deposit to Open: $0
• Bonus: N/A
• Fixed or Variable: Variable
• Monthly fees: None
• Best For: Checking + savings bundle
• FDIC Insured: Yes

SoFi
• APY: Up to 4.00%**
• Minimum balance for APY: None
• Access: Web/app
• Est. Earnings on $10K (1 yr): Up to $400
• Bonus: Up to $300 cash bonus
• Best For: Everyday banking + savings

LendingClub
• APY: Up to 4.00%***
• Minimum balance for APY: None (requires $250+/mo deposits)
• Access: Web/app; ATM card included
• Best For: Disciplined monthly savers

Marcus by Goldman Sachs
• APY: 3.50%
• Est. Earnings on $10K (1 yr): $365
• Best For: No-fee, no-strings savings

Synchrony
• APY: 3.40%
• Access: Web/app; optional ATM card; 400,000+ ATMs
• Est. Earnings on $10K (1 yr): $350
• Best For: Flexible access, no minimums

UFB Direct
• APY: 3.26%
• Access: Web/app; 90,000+ fee-free ATMs
• Est. Earnings on $10K (1 yr): $326
• Best For: ATM access without branch
• FDIC Insured: Yes (via Axos Bank)

American Express
• APY: 3.20%
• Est. Earnings on $10K (1 yr): $320
• Best For: Trusted brand, existing AmEx customers

Capital One 360
• APY: 3.10%
• Access: Web/app; branches; Capital One Cafés
• Best For: Branch access
* Promotional rate for Axos ONE bundle. Requires $1,500 monthly direct deposit and $1,500 average daily balance in checking; or $5,000 monthly deposits and $5,000 average daily balance. Base rate is 1.00% APY.
** SoFi's 4.00% includes a limited-time 0.70% APY boost for new members for up to 6 months (boost added to standard 3.30% APY with eligible direct deposit). Without direct deposit or qualifying deposits, savings earns 1.00% APY.
*** LendingClub LevelUp rate of 4.00% APY applies when $250 or more is deposited in the previous statement cycle's evaluation period. Standard rate is 3.00% APY.

What is a high-yield savings account?
A high interest savings account works like a traditional savings account. You deposit money, and your balance earns interest over time, but at a rate dramatically higher than you would get with a traditional savings account.
"Now is still a good time to open a high-yield savings account, as interest rates are still higher than they were during the COVID era, even though inflation pushed rates up quickly afterward. We are still seeing decent rates," Dana Menard, founder and lead financial planner at Twin Cities Wealth Strategies, Inc., says.
That rate difference generally comes down to overhead. Traditional brick-and-mortar banks pay for branches, staff and physical infrastructure, which are costs that eat into what they're able to offer depositors. On the other hand, most high-yield savings accounts come from online-only banks, which can and often do pass their leaner cost structure on to customers in the form of better rates.
In turn, the earnings gap between a top high-yield savings account and a conventional bank account can be substantial. On a $10,000 deposit, here's how the math works at today's rates:

Top high-yield savings account (Axos Bank)
• Rate: 4.21% APY
• Estimated earnings on $10,000 at the one-year mark: $421

National average
• Rate: 0.38% APY
• Estimated earnings on $10,000 at the one-year mark: $38

Typical big-bank savings (e.g., 0.01% APY)
• Rate: 0.01% APY
• Estimated earnings on $10,000 at the one-year mark: $1
Note: Savings yields differ depending on the bank. Earnings are rounded to the nearest whole number. National average per FDIC, May 2026.
It is important to note, however, that all savings account rates are variable, meaning they can rise or fall at any time without prior notice. If you want a rate that stays fixed, a certificate of deposit (CD) locks in your yield for a set term, though your money is less accessible during that period.
"Savers should take advantage of current rates by opening accounts now since nobody can predict what rates will ultimately do by year's end. Given the uncertainty the Iran War has brought into the market, with prices peaking, rates could possibly go down from where they are today. Plus, if rates rise later, high-yield savings accounts should adjust accordingly," Menard says.

Best high-yield savings accounts by category

Best high-yield savings rate: Axos Bank
Axos Bank's ONE bundle currently offers the highest APY on our list at 4.21%, but earning it requires some legwork. You'll need to meet a monthly direct deposit requirement and maintain a minimum average daily balance, which makes this a natural fit for people who are already using direct deposit and want to maximize every dollar in savings. The pairing with a checking account that earns its own competitive rate is a genuine perk, not just a marketing hook.
The catch, though, is that if you fall short of the deposit or balance requirements in any given month, your rate drops significantly to the base 1.00% APY. So, this account requires but ultimately rewards consistent behavior.

Best for everyday banking and savings: SoFi
SoFi's checking and savings combination account is a good example of why this financial institution is widely recognized as one of the best options for both bankers and savers. New members can earn up to 4.00% APY through a promotional rate boost for the first six months, and the base rate of 3.30% APY (with direct deposit) remains well above average once that window closes. There are no monthly fees, no minimums, and the app receives consistently high marks for usability.
The main limitation is that SoFi Savings functions as a companion to its checking product. That, in turn, means it's generally best suited for savers who want a unified financial home rather than a standalone savings vehicle.
Learn more about SoFi here.

Best for savers who deposit monthly: LendingClub
LendingClub's LevelUp Savings account is one of a small number of high-interest savings accounts that reward saving behavior, not just account balances. Deposit at least $250 into the account in a given statement cycle and you'll earn 4.00% APY on your entire balance. Miss that threshold and you'll still earn 3.00%, which is still competitive, but is also a meaningful drop.
LendingClub is also one of the rare online savings accounts that includes an ATM card with no ATM fees, which adds meaningful liquidity for savers who occasionally need cash access. Savers who can't reliably hit the $250 monthly deposit requirement, though, may find themselves toggling between rates month to month, which could be frustrating to track.

Best no-fee, no-minimum savings account: Marcus by Goldman Sachs
For savers who are skeptical of conditional rates or tired of reading fine print, Marcus delivers a genuinely clean proposition. This account strips away the friction points with no monthly fee, no minimum opening deposit, no minimum balance to earn the full APY and no cap on withdrawals or transfers. The 3.50% rate isn't the highest available, but it requires nothing beyond simply opening and funding the account.
The notable gap, however, is that Marcus offers no checking account and no ATM access, so it functions best as a dedicated savings vehicle paired with a primary checking accou

sources.excerpt: No-fee savings accounts essentially pay out more interest because you avoid having to pay any monthly fees. Here are today's best options.
sources.text:
9 Best No-Fee Savings Accounts of November 2026
Looking for a savings account without fees is important. Why give up your hard-earned cash and reduce your compounded earnings?
Fortunately, many high-yield savings accounts pay 8 to 10 times the national rate and don’t charge fees.
I’ve rounded up a list of all of the best no-fee savings accounts below and included what you need to know about each to decide to open one.

9 Best No-Fee Savings Accounts for November 2026
Here are the best no-fee savings accounts you can open today:
• Discover® Online Savings Account
• Synchrony Bank High Yield Savings
• Western Alliance Bank High-Yield Savings Premier
• Varo Online Savings Account
• Customers Bank High Yield Savings Account
• Sallie Mae HYSA
• CloudBank 24/7 Savings Account
• Marcus by Goldman Sachs High-Yield Savings
• GreenState Credit Union HYSA
Featured High Yield Savings Offer
Up to 4.15% APY + Signup Bonus: up to $1000 Bonus
Earn up to 4.15% APY on all balances with an HYSA through the Raisin Platform. You can also receive up to $1,000 signup bonus with qualifying activities!

1. Discover® Online Savings Account
• Minimum Deposit Requirement: $0
• Monthly Maintenance Fee: $0
Discover’s online high-yield savings account is the most transparent account out of the banks on our list. Like their credit card structure, Discover charges very few fees, making it easy to grow your savings faster.
Some of the fees Discover pledges not to charge include excessive withdrawals, expedited check delivery, stop payment, deposited item returned, insufficient funds, and account closure fees.
Plus, there’s no monthly maintenance fee to waive, and no minimum balance is required. They are unlike many other savings accounts that limit the number of monthly transactions before charging a fee or closing your account; they don’t have a limit.

2. Synchrony Bank High Yield Savings
Synchrony Bank offers a high-yield savings account online with no fees or minimum balance requirement. The Synchrony app makes it easy to bank from anywhere, and the account includes an ATM card for easy access to your funds, with ATMs showing the Plus or Accel logo.
Synchrony doesn’t charge a fee to use the ATM; however, the ATM owns it right, so always check.
You can deposit funds via external electronic transfer, internal transfer from a Synchrony account, mailed check, or direct deposit.
FDIC deposits are insured, and the APY is the same, no matter how much you deposit.

3. Western Alliance Bank High-Yield Savings Premier
• Minimum Opening Deposit Requirement: $500
• Account Activity or Maintenance Fees: $0
Western Alliance Bank, Member FDIC, has one of the most competitive high-yield savings accounts on the market, and it doesn’t have any account activity or maintenance fees.
The High-Yield Savings Premier is available through Western Alliance’s website.
You can easily link an external bank account to fund your savings account. Once you add your minimum opening deposit of $500, you’ll start earning the full APY on all your funds. The minimum balance required to earn APY is $0.01.

4. Varo Online Savings Account
• Minimum Deposit Requirement: None
Varo Bank is one of the first fintech companies to obtain a national bank charter. This allows them to offer FDIC insurance and more robust banking services, including a no-fee savings account.
Varo Bank makes it easy to save money by not charging any monthly fees or requiring minimum deposits. Better yet, your deposits are FDIC insured up to $250,000 to protect your money further.
Earn up to 5.00% APY on the first $5,000 saved if you have $1,000 qualifying direct deposits monthly and have an average daily balance of $5,000. Any balance above $5,000 earns 2.50% APY.
Open a No-Fee Savings Account with Varo

5. Customers Bank High Yield Savings Account
• Minimum Deposit Requirement: $1
Customers Bank has been in business since 2009, offering a variety of personal and business bank accounts.
It’s another solid choice if you’re looking for competitive interest rates and no monthly fees. The high-yield savings account from Customers Bank pays 11 times the national average savings rate.
You can apply for an account on the Raisin platform and link an external bank account to fund your savings account. Once you deposit $1, you’ll start earning interest, with no additional balance requirements or account tiers to worry about.
Currently, the account has no transaction limits or account fees, and your funds are FDIC-insured for up to $250,000.

6. Sallie Mae HYSA
Sallie Mae believes in helping young adults build their future, and not just with education loans. They offer robust savings programs to help your money grow with little to no fees.
The Sallie Mae High Yield Savings Account pays a high APY with interest compounded daily and paid monthly to help your money grow faster.
Sallie Mae HYSA funds are FDIC-insured, and no minimum balance is required.
The downside is they don’t have any physical branches, and customer service is only available during business hours, Monday to Friday, but online account management is always available.

7. CloudBank 24/7 High Yield Savings Account
CloudBank 24/7 should also be on your list if you’re looking for a fee-free high-yield savings account.
CloudBank 24/7 is the digital arm of Third Coast Bank, SSB, and it partners with Raisin to offer a truly fee-free savings account.
There are no requirements to earn the full interest rate beyond making a $1 minimum deposit. You can also make unlimited deposits and withdrawals from the account, which are processed in one to three business days.

8. Marcus by Goldman Sachs HYSA
Marcus by Goldman Sachs offers a high-yield savings account with no fees or no minimum deposit. They pay an APY 8 times the national rate and allow same-day transfers on amounts up to $100,000.
The Marcus app is intuitive and user-friendly, allowing you to make important financial decisions quickly. It takes only minutes to open an account, and you can link external accounts to transfer money.
Plus, their customer service center is available 24/7.

9. GreenState Credit Union HYSA
GreenState Credit Union is one of the country’s largest credit unions, and it’s open to members in all 50 states.
The High Yield Savings Account is one of its most popular products, with a competitive APY and a $1 minimum deposit. There are no monthly account fees or ongoing minimum requirements to earn the high-interest rate.
Rather than FDIC insurance, the account is insured by the National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) for up to $250,000.

What Is a No-Fee Savings Account?
No-fee savings accounts don’t charge monthly maintenance fees and offer high APYs with no monthly minimum balance requirements.
In other words, no-fee savings accounts allow you to make the most of your compounded earnings rather than giving them right back to the bank in the form of unnecessary fees.

How Do No-Fee Savings Accounts Work?
Most no-fee savings accounts are online, so you don’t have a brick-and-mortar bank to visit. But that doesn’t mean you must give up banking features to earn higher rates.
Online banks have just as many features as traditional banks, including robust mobile apps and the ability to use local ATMs to conduct some transactions.

Savings Compared to Common Account Fees
Online savings accounts typically don’t charge monthly maintenance fees, saving you up to $15 monthly, depending on the bank’s fees.
Most online banks also don’t charge other fees, such as non-network ATMs, overdrafts, or other miscellaneous fees.
The best thing about free online savings accounts is you don’t have to worry about dipping below a minimum balance. This is where most banks earn their money.
When customers’ bank account balances dip below the threshold, they charge a monthly maintenance fee. Even the most careful saver could forget or miscalculate, slip a few dollars below the threshold, and pay the fee.

How to Choose a No-Fee Savings Account
So how do you choose a no-fee savings account? A quick search online will turn up hundreds of options, but they aren’t all created equal.
Here are the top factors to consider when choosing a no-fee savings account.

Required Opening Deposit
Some banks require a specific opening deposit when applying for an account. The minimum may be low, like $5, but sometimes they are $250 or even $1,000. The higher the minimum opening deposit, the higher the bank’s APY.
If not, they may offer other unique services or benefits that other banks don’t offer. When choosing your bank, pay close attention to the requirements and what you get.

APY – Tiered or Regular?
One way some banks get you is with tiered interest rates. In other words, they advertise a high APY, but after you open an account, you realize you don’t meet the threshold to earn the higher APY and make much less interest.
Tiered APYs aren’t bad, but you must be able to meet and keep the minimum requirements to earn a higher rate. If you’re unsure

sources.text:
Comprehensive Analysis of Ally Bank’s High-Yield Savings Account Features and Benefits
Whether you are just starting to look for a bank to build your nest egg or you have an account and would like to consider better features, now is a good time to consider an online savings account.
Although you might be unsure of banking online versus the traditional method of brick and mortar banks, there are actually a number of reasons you could be better off with an online bank.
Further, you get the convenience of online and mobile banking, and the ability to speak with someone 24/7 if you need assistance. Plus, you can rest assured knowing your deposits are in good hands and FDIC insured.
Ally Bank is one of the biggest online banks in the U.S. and there’s a good reason for that: it offers accounts with low fees and high interest rates.
The Ally Online Savings Account is one of them. See if it can help you reach your savings goals faster.
In this Ally Bank Savings Account review, we’ll compare rates, fees and services to other national and online banks.

Ally Bank Online Savings Account Pros & Cons
• Earn a consistently high interest rate
• Great savings tools and features
• No monthly fees
• No branch or ATM access

Ally Interest Rates
One of the drawbacks of leaving your money in a big-bank savings account is that most aren’t paying enough interest to be worth it.
Fortunately, an Ally Bank savings account pays out one of the highest interest rates you will find with both online and major financial institutions.
Interest is also compounded daily, to allow you to earn interest on top of the interest that is added to your balance.
When compared to other leading banks, there really isn’t any competition.
For example, leading and well-known banks like PNC Bank, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Chase currently only offer interest rates of 0.01% on their basic savings accounts.
That means you can earn 100 times more interest with an Ally Bank savings account. It’s very clear that Ally Bank’s savings account will allow your money to grow significantly faster.

Buckets Feature
Ally Bank allows customers to assign nicknames to each account — in case you wanted to designate each account for a specific goal.
To make things even easier:
Ally offers the “Buckets” feature that allows you to label the funds in one account for multiple purposes, such as “emergencies” or “bill payments.”
It can help those who want additional organizational tools within their savings accounts.

Surprise Savings
Another nifty savings tool offer by Ally is the “Surprise Savings” program.
Basically, Ally will look at your checking accounts (whether the account is held with Ally or another bank) to identify room for additional savings.
If the program finds extra money that you can save, it will automatically transfer it to your Ally savings account.
Now:
Ally will request login information in order to analyze the checking account activity. Be sure that you’re comfortable with that.

Will You Need to Pay Fees?
You might find with online bank accounts that there are also fewer fees.
With the Ally Bank savings account, you don’t have to worry about paying a monthly maintenance fee or other hidden fees that you aren’t expecting.
This is one of the drawbacks that consumers face when searching for a new bank.
With major banks currently offering the lowest interest rates, it just doesn’t make sense to pay a monthly fee that can be as much as $10 or more every month. In fact, you risk the account costing you more than you earn in interest.

Other Fees to Consider
Although there aren’t any hidden fees or monthly maintenance fees to be aware of, there are other fees you might come across that aren’t as common. Other fees include:

Ally Savings Account Fees
Type of fee
Fee amount
Monthly Maintenance Fee
$0
Excess withdrawal (after 6 withdrawals in a month)
$10 each
Returned deposit item
$7.50
Overdraft item paid
$25 (limit once per day)
Expedited delivery fee
$15
Outgoing wire transfer (domestic)
$20
Research fee
$25/hour
Again, these are all fees that are rare and usually aren’t incurred on a regular basis.
The more standard fees like the monthly maintenance fee, ACH transfers, statement copies, and cashier’s checks are all $0.
This means, for the most part, you can build your savings account, without it costing you. And, you don’t have to worry about your earnings decreasing because of account maintenance expenses.

Transfer to Other Banks
It’s understandable that although you might choose to build your savings with Ally Bank, you might also have accounts with other financial institutions.
Fortunately, another feature of an Ally Bank savings account is the ability to transfer funds to another institution quickly and easily.
You can not only transfer funds between Ally bank accounts, but you can also transfer money between Ally Bank and other financial institutions, and you can even schedule transfers up to a year in advance.

Customer Service and Account Access
Many consumers today find that it’s difficult to live without the convenience of online and mobile banking.
Most online savings accounts provide both of these features so that you can access your bank account at any time, right from the convenience of your mobile device, tablet, or laptop.
You not only have access to your banking information 24/7 but with an Ally Bank savings account, you can also speak with someone 24/7.
This means you can contact customer service immediately by phone, chat, or email.
Plus, you can check the website for call waiting times to help you determine the best time to contact customer service. Most of the time, your wait time won’t be longer than one minute.

How Secure is Ally’s Savings Account?
If you are new to online bank accounts, you might wonder how safe your money actually is when you leave it with a bank that is only online.
Fortunately, banks like Ally are sometimes even more secure than others, and your deposits are FDIC-insured up to the maximum allowed by law.
Further, because it is an online bank, Ally has gone the distance to ensure that they can guarantee online and mobile safety.
You won’t be liable for any unauthorized transactions that are made online or through mobile banking, as long as you report the transaction within 60 days of when your statement is available to you.
If you still aren’t convinced, as a bonus, Ally Bank also offers free security software to protect up to three devices with Webroot SecureAnywhere software.
Plus, Ally uses features such as 2-step authentication and other security strategies, as well as fraud and identity theft tools and personal tips to help protect you from malware and other potential security concerns.

Compare to Other Online Savings Accounts
Ally Bank is a popular destination for people looking for great savings rates, but there are others that may come up during your search for an online savings account.

Capital One 360 Performance Savings
The online savings account from Capital One 360, Capital One’s online banking division, is very similar Ally’s savings account. It does offer a lower savings rate.
However, the 360 Savings account doesn’t charge excess withdrawal fees — the bank will just close your account if you do it too often. It also lets you create multiple accounts with nickname just like Ally.

Synchrony Bank High-Yield Savings Account
Synchrony Bank also offers an online savings account with an impressive savings rate with no minimum balance requirement. It comes with an optional ATM card and you can expect up to $5 refunded in ATM fees each month if you use non-branded ATMs.

Final Verdict: Great for All Savers
As you could probably guess, online savings accounts provide all the convenience and security you would expect from any bank.
Some of the best features, however, include one of the highest interest rates available from any bank, and no hidden fees.
With an Ally Bank savings account, you can save your money for college, an event, a vacation, or an emergency fund, and earn the most interest without paying ridiculous fees just to have the account.
Although there are many other traditional banking options as well as online banks like Ally, there isn’t any that can really compare when it comes to interest rates, fees, and features.
You already know you need a savings account, now you just need to find the right one for you and your family.
When you look at the Ally Bank savings account against nearly any other traditional bank or online bank, the others don’t quite stack up.

sources.excerpt: We’ve selected 10 savings accounts we think stand out in terms of a high APY and other important features.
sources.text:
Key Takeaways
• The best high-yield savings accounts in November 2026 offer APYs up to 4.21%, far higher than the national average, helping you grow your money faster with minimal risk.
• Top accounts typically feature low or no minimum balance requirements and minimal fees, making them accessible and cost-effective.
• High-yield savings accounts are ideal for building emergency funds or saving for short- to medium-term goals, giving you both strong interest earnings and easy access to your money.
A high-yield savings account (HYSA) is a foundational account that turns your dusty, stagnant money into a profitable workhorse. The average savings account earns a yawn-worthy 0.39%, per the FDIC, but the best high-yield savings accounts offer APYs (annual percentage yields) of up to 4.21% as of this writing.
If you want to earn interest on your money while still keeping it liquid enough to access in an emergency, putting those funds in a HYSA just makes sense. We’ve selected 10 savings accounts we think stand out in terms of a high APY and other important features such as rate caps and online banking. Read on for our top picks as well as comparisons to other types of accounts you might be considering.
Rates and bank details accurate as of July 29, 2026 and are subject to change.

Colorado Federal Savings Bank is headquartered in Greenwood Village, Colorado. It’s an online bank with few offerings in the way of deposit accounts—but it offers one of the most compelling high-yield savings accounts on the market.
Minimum balance required to earn APY
Minimum opening deposit
• Year Founded: 1990
• Company Headquarters: Greenwood Village, Colorado
• CEO: Matthew DeMarco

Why we picked Colorado Federal Savings Bank
A 3.80% APY is nothing to sneeze at. And with just a $1 minimum required to earn interest—with no monthly fees and no minimum opening deposit—this is a foolproof destination for your money. The bank also doesn’t enforce a cap on its impressive return rate, so it’s great for those with high balances.
Here’s the catch: Colorado Federal doesn’t offer a checking account or money market account. That means accessing your money will be slightly more cumbersome than having your checking and savings under the same roof. This is certainly a problem that can be overlooked for such high APY, but it’s worth noting.

Varo Bank
Founded in 2015, Varo Bank is online-only and offers products such as bank accounts and a credit card. As a neobank, it has over 3 million customers with a mission to make financial inclusion available to all.
• Year Founded: 2015
• Company Headquarters: San Francisco, CA
• CEO: Gavin Michael
Why we picked Varo Bank
At the time of writing, the account offers up to 3.75%. It’s got no monthly fees, meaning every dime you earn is essentially pure profit—and there’s a very accessible minimum deposit required to open an account. As long as you’ve got at least $0.01 in your account, you’ll earn interest.
That said, Varo has two sizable footnotes:
• You must receive qualifying direct deposits totaling $1,000 or more in your account each month.
• The 3.75% rate applies to a maximum balance of $5,000. Any money beyond that number will earn a less impressive 1.00%.
This makes this savings account best for those planning to keep a comparatively low balance in it.
A relatively new kid on the block, Vio Bank was established in 2018 as the online banking division of MidFirst Bank—the largest privately owned bank in the U.S. It specializes in savings, CDs, and money market accounts.
• Year Founded: 2018
• Company Headquarters: Oklahoma City, OK
• CEO: Todd Dobson (MidFirst Bank CEO)
Why we picked Vio Bank
Vio Bank’s impressive 4.00% APY applies to all balances with absolutely no extracurricular monthly activities necessary to earn it. There are no monthly fees, either. Vio does stipulate that you must deposit at least $100 to open an account, but that shouldn’t be an issue for most who are in the market for a high-yield savings account.
Vio Bank isn’t perfect for everyone, however. It doesn’t offer a checking account, so deploying your money isn’t as easy as with banks that allow you to instantly transfer funds between checking and savings. It does issue a money market account, but it doesn’t offer a debit card or check-writing privileges. In other words, you’ll need to transfer your money to an external bank before you can spend it.
Vio Bank is also fully digital, meaning there are no physical branches you can visit.
One of the rare financial institutions on this list with brick-and-mortar locations, EverBank manages to offer highly competitive APY without being one of those online-only banks with little-to-no overhead. It is headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, with its physical presence existing mostly in Florida, California, and New York.
• Year Founded: 1998
• Company Headquarters: Jacksonville, FL
• CEO: Greg Seibly
Why we picked EverBank
We think you won’t find a lower-maintenance high-yield savings account that’s more accessible than what EverBank has on offer. No minimum opening deposit, no monthly fees, no required monthly behavior to achieve its 3.90% APY.
Plus, its mobile app receives an impressive 4.7 stars on Google Play and the Apple App Store as of this writing—one of the highest ratings on our list. A solid online banking experience is an important factor to consider when deciding which HYSA to open.
Axos Bank is an online-only bank founded in 2000 that offers a range of personal and business banking products, including checking accounts, savings accounts, CDs, and loans.
• Year Founded: 1999
• Company Headquarters: San Diego, CA
• CEO: Greg Garrabrants
Why we picked Axos Bank
Axos Bank’s ONE savings account stands out for its high APY of up to 5.00%—currently the second highest return rate on this list. You’ll earn the full 5.00% APY on balances under $500,000. Any money above that will earn a slightly lower 4.01%.
This account has no monthly maintenance fees, but it is part of Axos Bank’s ONE program, which bundles checking and savings accounts together.
This bundled deal comes with an impressive checking account APY of 0.51%.
For the privilege of this high savings account return rate, you’ll need to achieve one of two things each month:
• Receive $1,500+ in total qualifying monthly deposits and maintain a minimum daily balance of $1,500+, OR
• Receive $5,000+ in total qualifying monthly deposits
If you fail to do this, you’ll earn a standard rate of 1.00% APY.
It’s also worth noting that Axos Bank offers expanded FDIC coverage of $2.5 million. That’s significantly more than you’d normally get from a bank, making this a better destination for big balances.
Originally founded as an online lending marketplace in 2006, Happen Bank has replaced San Francisco-based LendingClub. It offers a high-yield savings account—and it’s a good one.
Minimum opening depsoit
• Year Founded: 2006
• CEO: Scott Sanborn
Why we picked LendingClub
Happen Bank’s savings “LevelUp” savings account comes with an excellent 4.00% APY with no fees and no minimum balance. Its one minor annoyance is that you must deposit at least $250 into the account each month to earn that rate. If you don’t, you’ll earn a (still respectable) 3.00%.
This little detail makes Happen Bank’s savings account less of a set-and-forget option than many competitors.
A digital bank founded in 2020, ZYNLO Bank is part of PeoplesBank which is headquartered in Holyoke, Massachusetts. ZYNLO issues high-yield checking, savings, money market accounts, and CDs.
• Year Founded: 2020 (division of PeoplesBank which was founded in 1885)
• Company Headquarters: Holyoke, MA
• CEO: Tom Senecal
Why we picked ZYNLO Bank
Earning ZYNLO’s 3.85% APY with its Tomorrow Savings account is simple: Keep a minimum of $0.01 in your bank account. You won’t be subject to fees or throttled earning rates. Plus, ZYNLO does not enforce transfer limitations on its savings account. While many banks limit the number of transactions you can make with your savings account (often six per statement cycle), ZYNLO lets you transfer as often as you like.
It’s worth noting that ZYNLO Bank’s mobile app receives an average score of 3.75 across Google Play and Apple App Store reviews as of this writing. That’s far and away the lowest rating on Fortune’s list of top savings account options. The mobile banking experience is important—especially for a fully online bank with no option to service your account in-person. So, if you highly prioritize this factor, a different pick on our list might be better for your needs
